metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if recent price surged.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce forecast by 2–5% per subsequent day) post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±3σ of recent 7-day moving average.
- Model underestimates true price drops after prolonged high prices; add a “mean reversion” buffer: if 3 consecutive days > 45.00, forecast next day should be ≤ 42.00 unless event-driven.
- If true outcome shows a sudden drop after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply a “lag correction” rule: if true price drops > 5% from prior day, reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 3 days.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overfits to recent history; use 10-day rolling average as baseline, not 30-day forecast.
